validation.notes: Root cause: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() in packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts encoded the session directory with `.replace(/[/:]/g, "-")`, which never replaced backslashes and so diverged from the canonical encoder used by session-manager.ts and agent session repo.ts (`--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`). POSIX cwds happened to work, but Windows drive-letter cwds (C:\Users\alice\work\demo became `--C:\Users\alice\work\demo--` instead of `--C--Users-alice-work-demo--`) and UNC cwds (\\fileserver\team\share\demo became `--\fileserver\team\share\demo--` instead of `---fileserver-team-share-demo--`) were migrated into directories the session manager never reads, i.e. sessions appeared lost after migration. Fix is the one-token regex correction so all slash, backslash and colon characters are encoded to '-' after stripping exactly one leading separator, matching the canonical encoder byte-for-byte. No other behavior changed: session bytes are still moved with renameSync (no rewriting), invalid/foreign headers are still skipped, an existing destination is still never overwritten, and the file leaves the agent root so repeated runs are idempotent. Validation: `node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs` exits 0 (only Node's ExperimentalWarning lines on stderr). The regression loads the real migrations.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadMigrations (real fs/path, temp agentDir under .prale-eval) and asserts POSIX (/home/alice/work/demo -> --home-alice-work-demo--), drive-letter (C:\Users\alice\work\demo -> --C--Users-alice-work-demo--), forward-slash drive (D:/projects/app -> --D--projects-app--) and UNC (\\fileserver\team\share\demo -> ---fileserver-team-share-demo--) placement with byte-exact content (including a CRLF session), that non-JSON / wrong-type / missing-cwd headers stay untouched at the agent root, that a pre-existing destination file keeps its content and the colliding source stays put, and that two extra runs leave the whole agentDir tree byte-identical (idempotency). Differential check performed: reverting only the regex to the original `/[/:]/g` makes the script fail with `AssertionError ... C:\Users\alice\work\demo must migrate to .../sessions/--C--Users-alice-work-demo--`, so the regression is a real fault detector rather than a success print; the fix was then restored and the script re-run to green. Repo-wide vitest/biome were not run because node_modules is absent and installing dependencies is out of scope for this workspace, so the standalone Node 24 assertion script is the focused validation artifact.
